solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Might millions crack clues?

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

indicators.note: to crack something is to break it apart, so the letters of clues are broken up and reset

explanation.surface: A puzzle-lover wonders whether a fortune could buy the solutions to a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like 'solve', but it signals that the letters of 'clues' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Might as a noun is strength or power, and physical power is often called brawn or this word.

clue.text: Composer upsetting relative amateur

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: a ham is an amateur, especially a poor actor or a radio enthusiast

explanation.surface: A composer annoys a relative who plays music only as an amateur.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Mahler was the Austrian late-Romantic writer of symphonies.

clue.text: Always loveless, sour police died in service dress

indicators.note: love is zero, the letter O in tennis, and always means every instance of it is dropped

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died in records

explanation.surface: A gloomy story of unloved, sour police officers dying while in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O in tennis scoring; 'Always loveless' removes every O from the two words, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplice is the white vestment worn by clergy and choristers during a church service.

clue.text: Boxer Rebellion's central character succeeded after French agreement

indicators.note: the French yes comes after the middle letter
the central character is the single letter in the middle of the word Rebellion

parts.note: oui is French for yes
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A history lesson on the Boxer Rebellion in China and its leading figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer Rebellion' is a historical event, but Boxer is the definition: Joe Louis, world heavyweight champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Louis, the 'Brown Bomber', was world heavyweight champion from 1937 to 1949.

clue.text: Seeing the light from tail of test rocket

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, so only the end of test is used

parts.note: a rocket is British slang for a severe telling-off, as is a wigging

explanation.surface: Watching the glare from the back of a rocket during a launch test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocket' is not a missile but British slang for a dressing-down; WIGGING means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Twigging is British slang for suddenly understanding, so it is the same as grasping or realising.

clue.text: Nun's midwinter revels involving tango and saxophone?

indicators.note: says the letter is taken in among the other letters
revels as a verb means makes merry, so the letters cavort into a new order

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A nun celebrates in midwinter with a tango and saxophone solo.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is an example: a saxophone is one kind of this.
explanation.definitionFit: A saxophone is played by blowing, making it one of the woodwind family of instruments.

clue.text: Bungling cowboy docked on lake

indicators.note: in a down clue the cowboy is placed on top of the lake
a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a gaucho is a South American cowboy
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A clumsy cowboy has his boat moored on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' looks nautical beside 'lake', but means cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Bungling as a noun means clumsy, awkward behaviour, which is what this French borrowing describes.

clue.text: Silly sign painter forgetting odd letters

indicators.note: dropping the first, third, fifth letters and so on leaves the even ones

explanation.surface: A daft signwriter keeps forgetting some of the letters he is painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly and pointless or foolish are close synonyms.

clue.text: Sick mare gets better

indicators.note: sick means unwell or out of order, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A horse that was ill is recovering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as 'recovered' but is one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A better here is a punter who bets, and a gamester is a gambler.

clue.text: Wanderings of manic menopausal Brit

indicators.note: manic means frenzied and wild, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The rambling travels of a frantic British woman going through the menopause.
explanation.definitionFit: Perambulations are leisurely walks or strolls about, in other words wanderings.

clue.text: Female copper, slim and incredibly powerful

parts.note: her is the female pronoun
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
slim and lean both mean thin

explanation.surface: A description of a policewoman who is both slender and astonishingly strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but supplies the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercules was the mythical strongman, so a task or person named after him demands or shows immense strength.

clue.text: Remove weapons from section of lunar module

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Taking the guns off part of a spacecraft that lands on the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm someone is to take away their arms; this older verb carries the same sense.

clue.text: Ninety ducks do better than fish

indicators.note: to duck something is to dodge or avoid it, so the numeral is left out of the word

parts.note: to excel is to surpass or outdo
XC is ninety in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A boast that ninety ducks outperform a fish, perhaps at swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' looks like birds but is a verb meaning 'avoids': EXCEL avoids XC, leaving E, E, L.
explanation.definitionFit: This long snakelike creature is a familiar food fish, especially jellied in London.

clue.text: Servility ultimately brings luxury

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of brings is taken

parts.note: lavishness is extravagant luxury

explanation.surface: A moral that fawning obedience is rewarded with a life of luxury in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Servility is abject submissiveness, the attitude of someone behaving like a slave.

clue.text: Crust covering wings of angular beetle

indicators.note: the crust goes round, covering the letters that follow

parts.note: a scab is the crust that forms over a wound

indicators.note: wings are the outer parts, so the first and last letters of angular are used

explanation.surface: A beetle whose angular wings are covered in a hard crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings' suits a beetle but means only the outer letters A and R of 'angular', which go inside SCAB.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is the dung beetle held sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Disgusting dog adopted by extremely reclusive granny over time

indicators.note: in a down clue the granny sits above the time
the dog is taken into the family made by the other letters
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
a pug is a small dog breed

explanation.surface: A hermit's elderly grandmother takes in a revolting old dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by' puts the dog inside the reclusive granny's letters; in a down clue 'over' places her above the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repugnant is repellent or revolting, causing disgust.

clue.text: Can occupant eat on stairs regularly?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it
taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of stairs

parts.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a person sitting on the toilet might be eating there on the stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' suggests the toilet, but it is a tin; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: This small fish is famously sold packed tightly in tins.

clue.text: Fundamentally fashionable German city church

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
Essen is a city in the Ruhr
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A German city's church is, at bottom, a stylish place.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at heart or basically, so it is a synonym for fundamentally.

clue.text: Hungry masses invading empty farms

indicators.note: the masses move into the remaining pair of letters
an empty word has its inside removed, leaving only the first and last letters

parts.note: oodles means masses or lots

explanation.surface: Starving crowds overrun deserted farms in search of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A hungry person is without food, literally having nothing to eat.

clue.text: Something that defines single mate, over-attached to his mum?

definitions.note: an adjective describing a son too close to his mother

parts.note: the OED, the Oxford English Dictionary, defines words
I is the Roman numeral one
a pal is a mate or friend

explanation.surface: A dating profile: a single man looking for a partner, but rather too attached to his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Freud's complex is named after the king who married his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's complex describes a boy's desire for his mother, named after the mythical Theban king.

clue.text: Vein ought to be removed from shoulder joint

parts.note: a reef is a vein of ore, especially gold-bearing quartz

indicators.note: says the synonym is taken out of the word shoulder, leaving its remainder

parts.note: ought and should both express obligation

explanation.surface: Medical advice that a vein must be surgically taken out of a shoulder joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoulder joint' reads as anatomy, but 'joint' is the definition, meaning a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint is a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette, also called by this slang name.

clue.text: Pick up your foul uniform!

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up raises the letters, so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: yr is the written abbreviation for your
foul and evil both mean wicked

explanation.surface: A sergeant barks at a recruit to collect his filthy uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' sounds like an order, but it is the reversal signal for a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is the distinctive uniform worn by servants, staff or company employees.

clue.text: Durham gent's untidy drawers

indicators.note: something untidy is in disarray, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A gentleman from Durham, an English city, keeps a messy chest of drawers or messy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawers' suggests furniture or underpants, but here it means people who draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughtsmen make technical drawings, so they are literally those who draw.

clue.text: Aircraftman with weight and influence

parts.note: AC is the RAF abbreviation for aircraftman
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A junior airman with heft and clout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weight and influence' looks like a pair of nouns, but 'influence' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on something is to affect or have an effect on it.

clue.text: Foster son with energy to pursue rising career

indicators.note: the son and energy follow the reversed letters
in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards

parts.note: to career is to run headlong
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A boy named Foster and his energetic drive to climb his career ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' is a verb here, 'run fast'; RUN rising gives NUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster an idea or a child is to nurture or look after it.

clue.text: Briefly pelt runner

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's skin

explanation.surface: An instruction to throw things briefly at someone who is running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pelt' could be a verb meaning 'hurl' or 'run fast', but here it is a noun, the animal hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is a long narrow blade a sledge or snow vehicle glides on, such as one of a pair of these.

clue.text: Spear carrier on right shedding outer things

indicators.note: shedding its outer things means the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: dextral means on the right-hand side

explanation.surface: A soldier holds his spear in his right hand while stripping off outer garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on right' is a single idea, DEXTRAL; losing D and L leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear carrier is a walk-on actor with no lines, the theatrical term for a background performer.

clue.text: Navigation system, first of many now imaging in colour

indicators.note: says the other letters go inside the colour

parts.note: orange is a colour

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of many
a mirror image is reversed, so the word for now is turned round

parts.note: in means fashionable, of the moment, so now

explanation.surface: A navigation system that leads on many fronts by now producing images in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imaging' signals a mirror image, so the word for 'now' is turned round before going into the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnirange is a VHF radio beacon system that gives aircraft bearings in every direction.

clue.text: Censor opponents holding a demonstration back

indicators.note: the opponents hold the other letters between them

parts.note: South and East are opponents at bridge

indicators.note: back means the word for the demonstration is read backwards

parts.note: a sit-in is a protest demonstration

explanation.surface: Political opponents arrange a demonstration to restore something and stop censorship.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge South and East are partners of different pairs, so opponents; SITIN reversed is NITIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To censor material is to clean it up by removing objectionable content.

clue.text: Just one bank

parts.note: in crosswords, one, the speaker, gives me
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: Simply a single bank, perhaps a riverbank or a lender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a noun but is the verb 'rely', as in 'bank on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adverb means only or simply.
